children: flydubai is expanding its fleet beyond 100 aircraft and launching the next phase of its cabin retrofit programme in September, as the Dubai-based carrier strengthens capacity and upgrades its onboard offering.
The airline will receive 11 new aircraft in 2026, comprising seven Boeing 737-9 MAX and four Boeing 737-8 MAX.
The deliveries form part of its long-term fleet modernisation strategy, replacing older aircraft while providing greater flexibility to expand its network and increase capacity on high-demand routes.

Ghaith Al Ghaith, Chief Executive Officer at flydubai, said: “Growing our fleet beyond 100 aircraft is a significant milestone for flydubai and shows how far we have come. These deliveries are central to our long-term fleet strategy, providing the capacity and flexibility to support our growing operations while operating one of the youngest and most fuel-efficient fleets in the skies.”

Al Ghaith added: “Our investment does not stop with the new aircraft. We remain focused on enhancing our existing fleet, ensuring our customers enjoy a seamless and elevated experience when they travel with us. Our new retrofit programme marks another significant investment in our product offering and reflects our commitment to continuously enhancing the flydubai onboard experience.”
The Boeing 737-9 MAX aircraft will feature 16 Business Class and 156 Economy Class seats, compared with 10 Business Class seats on some 737-8 MAX aircraft.
The additional premium capacity is intended to meet demand for Business Class on key international routes and support higher-yield traffic.

From September, flydubai will also retrofit 21 aircraft over 12 months. Aircraft currently equipped with recliner Business Class seats will receive the carrier’s signature lie-flat seats, providing passengers with greater comfort.
The programme will also replace existing overhead bins with Boeing’s larger Space Bins, which can accommodate up to six standard-sized bags compared with four in standard bins.
The upgrade is expected to increase cabin baggage capacity and improve boarding efficiency.

The initiative builds on flydubai’s previous multimillion-dollar retrofit programme, which refreshed its Next-Generation Boeing 737-800 fleet with lie-flat Business Class seats, new Economy Class seating and inflight entertainment.
Together, the fleet expansion and cabin upgrades are designed to improve product consistency as the airline grows.

flydubai said its wider investment in technology, training and engineering infrastructure will support its future capabilities and strengthen Dubai’s position as a global aviation, trade and tourism hub.
